title: The Ballad of Sohlyngngem (Ka Ballad Ka Sohlyngngem)
cultural_context: The poetic ballad cycle of the green imperial pigeon (Sohlyngngem) mourning her separation from her beloved amidst the deep mountain gorges, from 'Ka Sohlyngngem U Oscar M. Wahlang'.

khasi: Ka Sohlyngngem ka rwai la ka sur;
Ba pynmih ia ki ummat kiba jaw;
Ka wad ia la u jied ba la jah,
Ha ki them bad ki riat ba dum;
Ha man ka janmiet ba kynjah.
english: High upon the bough of the pine tree,
The Sohlyngngem pigeon sings her plaintive melody;
A song of sorrow that pierces the soul,
Bringing forth tears that gently fall;
She seeks her lost beloved mate,
Across shadowed canyons and misty crags;

khasi: Wat la ki por ki la leit noh,
Ka jingieit jong ka kam ju tlot;
Ka shong marwei ha kliar u lum,
Ban ap ia ka jingshai ba thymmai;
To kan long ka dohnud jong ngi;
Ban ieit ia ka ri bad la ki kur
Ha ka hok ba pura junom.
english: Though years have drifted into the past,
Her faithful devotion never wavers or dims;
She perches alone on the mountain ridge,
Awaiting the dawn of a new sunrise;
So let our inner spirit be:
Loving our motherland and our kindred
In pure and unfaltering truth forever.

vocabulary.sohlyngngem: green imperial pigeon (emblem of tragic love in Khasi lore)
vocabulary.khu-ru: traditional onomatopoeia for pigeon's cooing call
